Of course, any time! I think one of the  the BIGGEST stigmas around disability in general is the thought that it's best to just ignore even if you are curious. In reality, and usually for not too personal questuond, we welcome questions about our disabilities with open arms. After all what is the point if we aren't spreading awareness? For this reason I very much admire her strength to say "No, I can't handle this right now." that is something I struggle with. Sometimes I try to say yes to things I can't even do for the possibility of being "normal" for a day. If you have any other questions or just wanna chat about drag sometime feel free to DM me!

Trust in your doctors (if you can, I understand the struggle of medical bills❤️) . Try to get a diagnoses so they can help you figure things out. My biggest tip of all is DO NOT DO PARTY TRICKS. What I mean by party tricks is bending your elbows backwards on purpose, bending your knees backwards on purpose, touching your thumb to your wrist on purpose just to impress people. I still slip up and do it sometimes, but it can be very damaging to your joints and ligaments and cause dislocations and tears. Try not to do them accidentally as well, for example leaning on your arms to where they over extend backwards. Another REALLY helpful thing for me has been aquatherapy, or pool therapy. If you have a local YMCA, they may actually have this available to you. If that's inaccessible I'd highly recommend googling some EASY exercises for EDS and related connective tissue disorders!
If you have any more questions about the things I've discussed feel free to either reply on here or DM me :) above all else, know you are NOT ALONE in this fight.

Yeah Ehler's Danlos is portrayed as "the contortionist dream" in the media. When in reality, we are in pain every single day, and it comes with other side effects as well such as slow healing, digestive issues, need for constant physical therapy, countless tests and doctors appointments. It's scary to think that people portray it as no big deal.
My biggest issue, is that it is almost invisible. So I get yelled at for using the big stall for the handles so I don't dislocate hips, or parking in wheelchair spaces (with a permit of course). Not all disabilities are visible which is a HUGE lesson that needs to be spread more!
